experiences.title: Morning Light: A Shared-Caregiving Digital Single-Session Intervention for School Refusal
experiences.summary: Developing a culturally adapted, caregiver-focused intervention that addresses both pressure and accommodation in responses to school refusal.
bullets: Reviewed 61 studies to inform a 25–30-minute mobile prototype adapted from Project EMPOWER for Chinese caregivers.
Designed content on distress tolerance, validation, and graded return-to-school steps, with safety triage and a three-minute pathway for a second caregiver.
Planned parent co-design and a pilot randomized trial, including evaluation of the second-caregiver pathway. The prototype has not yet been evaluated in a trial.
Received Second Prize in a national academic paper-writing competition and presented a poster in Jinan in October–November 2026.

experiences.title: Social and Academic Self-Concept Profiles in Preadolescence
experiences.summary: Examining cross-sample profile stability and prospective within-child links across self-concept domains.
bullets: Reanalyzed four-wave data from Taiwan (Grades 5–6; N = 1,016) and used U.S. Early Childhood Longitudinal Study data (Grades 3 and 5; N = 14,392 and 11,282) to examine replication.
Applied latent profile and transition analyses to study five self-concept profiles and their stability.
Used random-intercept cross-lagged panel models, adjusting for global self-worth, to examine prospective associations between peer acceptance and other self-perceptions.

experiences.title: Active Ingredients of Self-Recording: Daily Mood in a Lockdown Photo-Diary Intervention
experiences.summary: Investigating everyday experiences associated with mood in a self-designed, single-arm photo-diary program for emerging adults.
bullets: Analyzed 12,799 diary entries from 681 accounts over 28 days, with matched pre–post assessments for 442 participants.
Developed semantic codes through two mood-blind coding passes before linking diary content to mood ratings.
Within-person analyses in Python examined associations of nature, pets, and food sharing with same-day mood. The single-arm design does not establish causal intervention effects.
Submitted a poster abstract to the 2027 Global Stress & Resilience Meeting; decision pending.

experiences.title: Adolescent School Refusal in China: From Family Interviews to Policy
experiences.role: Interviewer | Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
experiences.summary: Qualitative work with the National Mental Health Assessment and Development Center.
bullets: Interviewed a family facing school refusal and prepared verbatim transcripts and a reflexive log.
Authored a policy brief proposing ten school- and community-level measures with evaluation indicators.

experiences.title: Eating for Whom? Food Posts and Identity Construction Among Chinese Young Adults
experiences.role: Trainee Researcher & Group Presenter | Shanghai Normal University
experiences.summary: Digital fieldwork on food sharing, relationships, and self-presentation.
bullets: Conducted and thematically analyzed 14 photo-elicitation interviews and piloted a pre–post self-esteem measure.
Examined how food posts communicate relational ties and how concerns about appearing boastful shape self-presentation.
Received an individual First Prize Scholarship and presented a group study based on 64 interviews.

experiences.title: Adapting the Trauma Recovery and Empowerment Model (TREM)
experiences.role: Research Assistant & Group Recorder | National Taiwan University
experiences.summary: Supported a localized group intervention for incarcerated women with substance-use and trauma histories.
bullets: Co-screened participants and rehearsed plans for the localized 12-session program; independently facilitated one session at Taoyuan Women’s Prison.
Documented and analyzed 15 group sessions using structured dialogue, nonverbal observations, and group-process frameworks.
Collected pre–post assessments for 19 women across two prison cohorts and interviewed five participants; contributed to a longitudinal evaluation (N = 59) with follow-up through ten months.

experiences.title: School-Based Social-Emotional Learning and Self-Concept Development
experiences.role: Research Assistant & Project Coordinator | National Taiwan University
experiences.summary: Coordinated longitudinal evaluation of social-emotional learning curricula in Taiwan and Beijing.
bullets: Managed data from a six-wave Taiwan study with 1,700+ participants and a two-wave Beijing study with 2,300+ participants.
Used Mplus and R for factor analysis, latent growth models, and multi-group autoregressive latent trajectory models; used SPSS and SAS for emotion-regulation analyses.
Developed a coding system with Prof. Lay and recruited and trained five undergraduate coders.
Completed an A+ master’s thesis and contributed to three ENSEC 2019 poster presentations.

experiences.title: Maternal Beliefs and Preschoolers’ Motivational Choices
experiences.summary: Graduate scientific-writing seminar research using data from 77 mother–child dyads.
bullets: Conducted reliability, correlation, regression, and moderation analyses in SPSS and R and drafted a preliminary English course manuscript.

experiences.title: Visitor Expectations and Experiences in a Safari Park
experiences.role: Undergraduate Thesis Researcher | Sun Yat-sen University
experiences.summary: Mixed-methods research on visitor behavior and educational experiences.
bullets: Combined observations of 507 groups across six exhibits, 44 pre-visit interviews, and 600 verbal records with hierarchical regression analyses.

experiences.title: Education and Adolescent Development in Rural Yao Communities
experiences.role: Field Research Intern | Sun Yat-sen University
bullets: Used participant observation, interviews, and case analysis to study rural adolescents and left-behind families; final report graded 92/100 (Excellent).
